standard_prerequisites.name: Rational maps of varieties and function fields
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the equivalence between (1) and (2) by restriction: a variety is a curve exactly when its function field has transcendence degree 1.

standard_prerequisites.name: Extension of morphisms from the generic point
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemmas lemma-extend-over-normal-curve and lemma-extend-over-dvr; Varieties, Lemmas varieties-lemma-dim-1-proper-projective, varieties-lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic, varieties-lemma-reduced-dim-1-projective-completion
standard_prerequisites.use: Extends a rational map from a normal curve to a morphism, and produces the normal projective model of a given function field by normalizing and completing.

core_obligations: Identifications (proof lines 393-407): categories (3), (4), (5), (6) coincide because regular and nonsingular are synonyms and normal equals regular in Noetherian dimension 1, while normal proper curves are projective (varieties-lemma-dim-1-proper-projective).

Fully faithful functor (5) -> (1) (proof lines 409-425): a nonconstant morphism of nonsingular projective curves sends the generic point to the generic point, giving k(Y) -> k(X); two morphisms inducing the same field map are equivalent rational maps, hence equal by lemma-extend-over-normal-curve; conversely a field map gives a morphism on an open which extends over all of X by lemma-extend-over-dvr.

Essential surjectivity (proof lines 427-445): every K/k of transcendence degree 1 is k(X) for a curve X; normalize to assume X normal, then take the projective completion with complement {x_1, ..., x_n}; the local rings at the x_i are normal, so the completion is a normal projective curve (with the author's remark on the alternative order of compactify-then-normalize avoiding the tricky relative normalization lemma).
proof_roadmap: Restate (1) equivalent (2) by the varieties-level theorem, restricted by transcendence degree.
Collapse (3), (4), (5), (6) by the dimension-1 regular-normal dictionary and projectivity of normal proper curves.
Build the fully faithful functor from nonsingular projective curves to function fields via generic points and the two extension lemmas.
Produce the normal projective model of any given function field by normalization plus projective completion.
difficulty_reason: The theorem is the backbone classification of curves by function fields (statement lines 375-387). The proof (lines 389-445) assembles the equivalence in three moves: the variety-level rational map equivalence restricted by transcendence degree, the dictionary among the four curve categories, and the construction of the fully faithful functor plus essential surjectivity through the extension lemmas and the normalization-completion construction, including the author's closing remark on the alternative order of the last two steps. H2: each move is a reference chase with one genuine construction (the normal projective model), the whole being a canonical-equivalence proof rather than a computation.
